content: Bottom bar + More sheet mapping: platform guidance (Material 3 navigation bar, iOS HIG tab bar) supports a small number of primary destinations (3-5) with an active-destination indicator; overflow destinations go to a secondary surface (drawer/sheet/More tab). m3.material.io content is JS-rendered and unfetchable, so the 3-5 figure is established practice rather than a fetched quote. For a client-routed React app the mapping is structurally safe: routes stay identical (NavLink to the same paths), the bottom bar and the More sheet are just two renderings of the same route list, and deep links keep landing on the same Route elements — the switch is presentation-only in the Layout shell. Active tab = current location.pathname match, which NavLink already computes.
